title: Spread the work across cores
prompt: The platform team wants three tasks per core when it processes `api_requests`. This program sizes the partitions from the cores Spark has. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
cores = spark.sparkContext.defaultParallelism
spread = api_requests.repartition(cores * 3)
print(cores)
print(spread.rdd.getNumPartitions())
print(spread.count() / spread.rdd.getNumPartitions())
hints: Spark here runs as `local[2]`, and `defaultParallelism` follows the number of cores.
The last line divides the number of requests by the number of partitions, with Python's `/`.
explanation: `defaultParallelism` is 2, one per core, so `repartition(6)` makes 6 partitions. The 12 requests are only moved around, so on average each partition holds `12 / 6` = `2.0` rows; Python's `/` always gives a decimal number.
